title: Shipping label creation with carrier error wrapping
name: Shipping label service

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code wraps carrier errors and preserves their context? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The carrier answers one label request with HTTP 400. How many times does _request_label call the carrier, and what does process_batch record for that shipment?
choices: Four times, then a failure entry named LabelError
Once, then a failure entry named CarrierRejected taken from the exception chain
Once, and the 400 propagates out of process_batch because only LabelError is caught per shipment
Once, then a failure entry named HTTPError because root_cause follows the chain to the requests exception

questions.prompt: In CarrierClient.create_label, why is `from exc` used on each raise?
choices: It makes the new exception inherit from the requests exception class so existing handlers still match
It records the original exception as __cause__, so tracebacks show it as the direct cause and code walking the chain can find it
It suppresses the original exception so callers only see the domain error
It re-raises the original exception after the domain exception has been logged

questions.prompt: While building the payload in LabelService.create_label, a shipment dict turns out to lack the 'weight_g' key. What happens in process_batch?
choices: The shipment is recorded in failures with root cause KeyError and processing continues
A KeyError propagates out of process_batch, abandoning the remaining shipments and discarding the labels collected so far
tenacity retries the KeyError up to four times and then raises LabelError
The KeyError is converted into a CarrierRejected by the client
